description: Repair a corrupted Type-2 history of employee department assignments so that, per employee, versions are unique, contiguous and non-overlapping. Steps: (1) when several rows share (employee_id, valid_from), keep only the one with the latest loaded_at; (2) merge consecutive versions (ordered by valid_from) that have the same department into one version starting at the earliest valid_from; (3) recompute valid_to as the next version's valid_from (ignoring the stored valid_to, which may overlap or leave gaps); the last version has valid_to NULL. Only employees present in the employees table are kept. Output columns: employee_id (INT64), department (STRING), valid_from (DATE), valid_to (DATE). Sort by employee_id, valid_from.

valid_to.description: Version end (exclusive); NOT trustworthy - overlaps and gaps exist

loaded_at.description: When the row was written; reloads created duplicates

edge_cases: Analytics originally overlaps Billing by one month; its valid_to is pulled back to 2024-05-01
Duplicate (employee, valid_from) rows from a reload collapse to the latest loaded_at
Two consecutive Billing versions (2024-05-01 and 2024-07-01) merge into one
The stored gap between 2024-09-01 and 2024-10-01 is closed by extending Billing to 2024-10-01
common_failure_modes: FM3: Computing LEAD(valid_from) before removing duplicates and merging identical neighbours yields zero-length or fragmented versions
FM3: GROUP BY employee_id, department to merge versions also merges non-adjacent periods (A -> B -> A)
FM7: No post-check that versions are non-overlapping and that exactly one open-ended row exists per employee
